captions.detailed: This 3D model is a replacement ground stake designed for solar garden lights. It features a long, tapered four-fin point that converges to a blunt tip at the bottom, providing structural strength for insertion into the soil. At the top of the point, a flat circular divider flange transitions to a cross-shaped (plus-sign) mounting riser. The cross-shaped riser includes an integrated horizontal ring segment near its top, designed to friction-fit securely inside a tubular garden light pole.
captions.instruction: Design a parametric solar light replacement stake in OpenSCAD. The stake must feature a blunt, four-finned tapered ground point and a cross-shaped top riser with an integrated collar ring, allowing users to customize dimensions such as point length, top radius, fin thickness, and riser width.
captions.factory: The code constructs the ground stake using three main sections assembled with a union. The bottom section is created by rotating four extruded 2D polygons (triangles with a subtracted square at the tip) at 90-degree intervals to form the four-finned point. A thin cylinder acts as the circular divider flange at the top of the point. The top riser is built by intersecting a cross shape (made of two perpendicular squares) with a circle, extruding it, and unioning it with a thin extruded circle offset near the top.
